messages:
maria: heads-up: production incident - tenant with geo-restrictions had writes rejected after a routing cache bounce. client session hit a frontend that routed to a shard in a different region; serving layer denied. anyone seen this exact flow?
ajay: yes. routing catalog and serving residency drift during quick promotions. cache TTLs too long for our failover window.
leila: is this tied to fast rebalances? we usually allow sub-minute cache staleness to avoid thundering.
samir: correct. fast rebalance + routing caches cause a narrow window where routing thinks shard A is primary in region X but serving already moved to region Y. legal checks compare request region -> reject.
maria: short-term mitigation: prevent non-drain promotions for tenants with residency_policy=STRICT; force a drain handoff. ops PR to roll this today?
ajay: +1. medium-term: add a session-scoped region-assertion token minted by control-plane at session creation or explicit handoff. routing attaches token to internal calls; serving verifies token.region == its region. token small, signed (ed25519), TTL ~ 60-180s.
leila: compliance: tokens must not include PII. define "region" semantics in RFC (cloud region id vs legal jurisdiction). also decide default-on-verify-fail: deny for EU clusters, log-only elsewhere during canary.
samir: implementation notes: proxies/serving nodes cache validated tokens per-session until expiry to avoid per-request crypto. public keys pulled periodically; tokens carry key-id to pick verifier. key-rotation overlap window required.
maria: telemetry: token_verify_fail, token_region_mismatch, promotion_blocked_by_cache_miss. alert threshold suggestion: token_region_mismatch > 0.05% over 5m.
ajay: I'll prototype a tiny verify lib + LRU token cache in the proxy runtime (2 days). samir, can you spec mint API and operator runbook for emergency key rollback?
samir: will do. include load test numbers for verify latency + cache hit tradeoffs. add a safe fallback: if verification service unreachable, cluster-config decides deny vs allow.
leila: legal will review RFC for region taxonomy and fallback policy. we'll prioritize deny for tenants with contractual residency obligations.
maria: action items: RFC draft "region-assertion token" (maria), proxy verify spike (ajay), mint API + runbook (samir), compliance review (leila). I'll open the ops PR to force-drain STRICT tenants now and post links in 48h. :thumbsup:
legal-bot: Note: flagged for legal review - please include jurisdiction mapping and customer-facing failure modes in RFC.
